entrypoints.summary: A caller reaches Array::insert with a key type whose user-provided K::compare implementation can panic during insertion.

affected_components.role: Pre-fix insertion code writes key/value snapshots and later invokes the caller-controlled comparison method.

code_slices.fixed: The supplied patch uses ManuallyDrop and explicitly extracts values on paths that return them to the caller rather than relying on a later mem::forget.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The advisory states that node-split handling was also reorganized from insert to insert_try followed by insert_unchecked.
code_slices.vulnerable: The insertion path writes snapshots to the data block, calls K::compare, and performs mem::forget only after insertion completes.

negative_controls: Use a compare implementation that does not panic.
observability.positive_marker: The reports predict double free during unwind; this bundle does not contain an observed runtime marker.

preconditions: The application uses an affected scc version prior to 3.8.4.
A caller can invoke Array::insert with a key type implementing a compare method that panics.
Panic behavior unwinds rather than immediately aborting the process.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A generic key type implementing K::compare to deliberately panic.
trigger_steps.summary: Call Array::insert with a key whose comparison callback panics after the insertion path has written key and value snapshots.

impact.affected_asset: Heap-managed ownership represented by inserted key and value and their snapshots in the array data block.
impact.attacker_capability: A library caller able to supply a K implementation whose compare method panics can trigger the described unwinding path while calling Array::insert.
impact.security_effect: Rust memory-safety soundness violation with potential double free during panic unwinding.

causal_trace.summary: Array::insert invokes the user-provided K::compare method while processing the insertion.
On the UPSERT path, snapshots of key and value are written into self.data_block before insertion completes, while ownership suppression via mem::forget occurs only later.
If K::compare panics before mem::forget, stack unwinding runs destructors for key, value, and self despite snapshots already residing in the data block.
The overlapping destruction paths can double free owned data; the advisory also states analogous behavior in the non-UPSERT path.

failure.operation: Panic unwinding invokes destructors for duplicated ownership representations, producing a potential double free.

primary_invariant.statement: Once key and value are snapshotted into the array, panic unwinding must not drop both the original values and the array-owned snapshots.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix implementation stores snapshots, subsequently executes fallible user comparison code, and defers mem::forget until after that code returns.

quality.review_notes: The advisory, issue source excerpt, and merged remediation material consistently describe the ownership/unwinding mechanism and fixed release. No executable regression test, build command, sanitizer output, or observed crashing run is present in this bundle, so reproducibility and deterministic triggering are not established here. The upstream commit page itself was bot-interstitial content; remediation evidence is grounded in the supplied diff, advisory, and merged PR material.

remediation.invariant_restored: Key and value are wrapped so unwind cannot run their ordinary destructors after their ownership has been transferred into the array; values are explicitly recovered only on return paths that retain caller ownership. The advisory additionally describes splitting insertion into insert_try followed by insert_unchecked for node splitting.
mitigation_classes: separation of fallible insertion work from infallible node-split work

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Supply a key type whose comparison callback panics during the post-snapshot comparison phase.
data_structure_invariants: Snapshots in self.data_block must have one unambiguous destruction owner.
An unwind through user-supplied comparison code must preserve ownership safety.
state_context.state_machine: Array insertion may reserve/write a data-block position, compare the supplied key against stored keys, then either return ownership on a failure/full path or complete transfer on success.
